---
name: Scope enquiry
about: Ask whether a class of problem falls within SIGNET's intended scope. Use this when the expected answer may be "no", or when the answer is needed before a change proposal can sensibly be written.
title: "SE: <short description of the problem class>"
labels: scope-enquiry
---

<!-- A scope enquiry is not a change proposal and not a defect. It asks the Foundation to determine a boundary. It may be answered: in scope (core), in scope (extension), in scope (companion standard), out of scope, or deferred pending a stated condition. Every answer is recorded with reasoning so the question cannot be re-raised without new argument. -->

## The problem class

<!-- What is not currently expressible, and why it is a boundary question rather than an implementation choice. Two or three paragraphs. -->

## Evidence that the gap is structural

<!-- Why no existing open standard fills it, and why a local solution reproduces the asymmetry the standard exists to remove. -->

## What is asked

<!-- The determination requested. If a candidate approach exists, link it; do not restate it here. -->

## Declared interests

<!-- Role-based. Do not name individuals or commercial implementers. e.g. "The enquirer is a deploying implementer with an operational interest in the outcome." State any recusal requested. -->

## Dependencies already known

<!-- Open defects, pending decisions, or prerequisites this enquiry depends on or exposes. -->

## Suggested disposition

<!-- Optional. The enquirer's own view of where the answer should land, and what could proceed without the determination. -->
